- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) within 5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion zones when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias if 3+ consecutive days show sentiment ≤0.50.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights recent sentiment; weight last 7 days’ sentiment 3x more than older days when adjusting for horizon-specific drift.
- If true outcome deviates >1.5% from forecast in first 5 days, model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days.
